text:
sara.ops: Quick heads-up — ran the week-ahead GPU bakeoff against the eu-west fleet this morning. Found a repeatable pattern where short spikes (1–3m) trigger burst scaleups but then we hit a softcap and requests queue for ~60–120s. Full notes attached in thread below.

cheng.runtime: Can you paste the key metrics? p99, ramp time, and how often softcap kicked in.

sara.ops: Sure. High level: p50 latency unchanged, p95 up 12%, p99 up 28%. Burst scaleup executed in ~35s, but softcap prevented full node allocation for 4/7 test runs, causing queue backlog to climb and median token throughput drop ~18%. Softcap condition triggered when reserve_ratio <= 0.12 for sustained_window=90s.

elena.sre: That matches a few production incidents last month. We tuned softcap to avoid noisy scaleups during short blips, but it seems too aggressive at current traffic shapes.

mike.infra: What were the config values used in the test?

sara.ops: Test policy snippet we used: 
```
autoscale:
  burst_multiplier: 1.5
  soft_cap_ratio: 0.12
  sustained_window_sec: 90
  max_burst_nodes: 15
```

ben.finance: Rough cost delta? If we reduce the softcap we may increase monthly GPU hours. Need a quick estimate.

sara.ops: Short-run numbers from the bakeoff: reducing soft_cap_ratio from 0.12 -> 0.08 cut tail-queue time by 70% and restored throughput, but increased overprovisioned GPU-hours in spike windows by ~9% for the test day. Annualized that’s ~+3% on eu-west committed hours if spikes follow current pattern.

elena.sre: Proposals: (1) lower soft_cap_ratio to 0.08 and keep sustained_window at 90s, (2) introduce a transient-grace window: allow 1 immediate small burst (up to 2 nodes) even if softcap is hit, and (3) bump monitoring alert to track queue_time > 45s. Thoughts?

cheng.runtime: I like the transient-grace idea — lets us handle sub-minute flares without full scale. Implementation suggestion: treat first burst as provisional; if queue backlog not decreasing after 60s, then rollback that provisional allocation.

mike.infra: We should also add a conservative per-region headroom floor for scheduled events (campaigns, promos). For EU we can reserve 6% baseline headroom during peak hours (08:00–20:00 UTC) to reduce churn.

ben.finance: If we reserve headroom, does that change the committed-reserved mix? We might need to adjust forecasts before next renewal. Need numbers.

sara.ops: I'll produce a 7-day sim matrix: current vs softcap 0.08 vs softcap 0.08 + transient-grace + 6% reserve. Will include GPU-hours, estimated overprovision percentage, and expected p99. ETA EOD.

autoscale-bot: [simulation-run] eu-west bakeoff 2026-03-17 10:12 UTC — results uploaded to /shared/infra/bakeoffs/eu-west/1802003456/

elena.sre: Nice. Small ask — can the sim include a scenario with burst_multiplier=1.3? We saw some traffic patterns where 1.5 overshoots and leaves idle capacity after spikes.

cheng.runtime: Agree. Lowering burst_multiplier + transient-grace might hit a sweet spot: less overshoot, faster response to real sustained demand.

mike.infra: Operational note — if we change softcap we should update the runbook for oncall: guidance on when to manually force scale and when to let policies run. Also add a post-change watch period: 72h with reduced alert thresholds.

ben.finance: Okay, hold on formal approval until sim and 72h cost estimate are in, but I’m open to the transient-grace + slight reduction in softcap if the cost delta stays <5% annualized for eu-west.

sara.ops: Great. Action items: 1) I’ll upload sims with the variants (softcap 0.08, transient-grace, burst_multiplier 1.3/1.5) by EOD. 2) @mike.infra to draft runbook update and watch-period plan. 3) @elena.sre to add the queue_time >45s alert and a dashboard tile. 4) @ben.finance to review cost sim and respond tomorrow.

cheng.runtime: Perfect — thanks. If sims confirm, we can roll canary to 2% traffic in eu-west for 48h before wider rollout.

mike.infra: Will start the runbook draft and post a PR.

ben.finance: I’ll review sims tomorrow morning.

sara.ops: Thanks all. I'll ping when sims are up. :thumbsup:
